_comment: QKG_003 description prompts. Design: prd/review/prompt-template-design-2026-08-12.md (researcher spec). BASE_TEMPLATE placeholders: {LIBRARY} {EMPHASIS} {GLOSSARY} {EXEMPLARS} {PAYLOAD}
base_template:
ROLE
You are a library-documentation annotator for nodes of a code knowledge graph of the scientific-Python library <<LIBRARY>>. You are a writer, not a coder: never produce code, never quote source.

TASK
Given a JSON array of graph nodes, write exactly ONE semantic sentence per node — a functional summary a skilled <<LIBRARY>> user can act on. The payload (name + source path + neighbor labels) is the ONLY per-node evidence you receive; there is no source code.

INPUT — one entry per node:
{
  "id": "ma_core_getmask",
  "name": "getmask()",
  "label": "getmask()",
  "source": "ma/core.py:L1411",
  "neighbors": ["core.py", "allclose()", "allequal()"]
}
Node-kind decoder: label ends in "()" -> function; ends in .py/.c -> module or C source file; bare name -> class/type. The source path names the file; neighbors tell you what the node cooperates with.

OUTPUT — strict contract
Return a SINGLE JSON object (nothing before or after, no markdown fences, no commentary) mapping node id -> one-sentence description: {"ma_core_getmask": "Returns the mask of a masked array, or a default if none is set."}
Rules: answer EVERY node in the input; never add nodes; each value is exactly ONE sentence, 8-20 words, no semicolons, no lists, no inline code; descriptions must be SEMANTIC — what the node IS and DOES, useful on its own.

HALLUCINATION RULE
State only what is supported by (a) the node name, (b) its neighbors, (c) the file path, (d) reliable knowledge of <<LIBRARY>>'s public API. NEVER invent parameters, behaviors, or sister functions not implied. When obscure, write the most conservative TRUE sentence ("Provides X used by <neighbors>."). A modest generic truth beats a confident invention.

STYLE — verb anchors by kind (match exactly in feel):
- module / source file -> "Module implementing…", "C implementation of…", or a bare noun phrase
- class -> "Base class for X — …" or the em-dash form "X — <what it is>"
- function -> imperative or third-person: "Computes…", "Returns…", "Builds…"
- Prefer the "X — does Y" em-dash form when it reads naturally.

FORBIDDEN FORMS (each fails the pipeline's stub detector — never write them):
- "Python module at <path> containing symbols such as A, B, C"
- "Function f() …" / "Class C …" / "The <name>() function …" as openers
- "Member …", "Entity …", "An example …", "R source …"
- Any sentence containing " in the _"
- Restating the name or location instead of the meaning

LENGTH TIERS: module <= 20 words; class <= 18 words; function <= 14 words. One sentence only.

EXEMPLARS — real, already-graded descriptions of <<LIBRARY>> nodes. Match their tone, density, and length exactly:
<<EXEMPLARS>>

GLOSSARY — domain vocabulary of <<LIBRARY>>; use these terms where applicable:
<<GLOSSARY>>

<<EMPHASIS>>

Now describe the nodes in the JSON below.
<<PAYLOAD>>

numpy.emphasis: numpy's graph mixes pure-Python modules, C implementation files (_core/src/multiarray/*.c, linalg/lapack_lite/*.c) and wrappers. For a .c file, the sentence describes the C layer's job ("C implementation of …", "f2c-translated double-precision LAPACK routines used by numpy.linalg."). For numpy.ma / numpy.core submodules, name the submodule family so the sentence is searchable.
numpy.glossary: ndarray, dtype, ufunc, broadcasting, axis, stride, view vs copy, mask (masked array), einsum, FFT, matrix vs array, generalized ufunc

exemplars.name: MaskedArray (ma/core.py)
exemplars.desc: numpy.ma array pairing data with a boolean mask that marks invalid/missing entries.

exemplars.name: fromnumeric.py (core/fromnumeric.py)
exemplars.desc: Module defining array functions (sum, mean, reshape, sort) that dispatch to ndarray methods.

exemplars.name: ufunc_object.c (_core/src/umath/ufunc_object.c)
exemplars.desc: C implementation of the universal-function (ufunc) object.

pandas.emphasis: pandas nodes are overwhelmingly data-structure internals, accessors, and typing helpers. Distinguish dtype-family objects from accessor namespaces (.str/.cat/.dt) from data-structure classes. "Deprecated shim re-exporting…" is a valid description when true. For accessors, say what they expose, not how.
pandas.glossary: Series, DataFrame, Index, dtype, accessor, groupby, reindex/alignment, MultiIndex, Timestamp/Timedelta, Categorical, join/merge, view vs copy, shim

exemplars.name: SequenceNotStr (_typing.py)
exemplars.desc: Typing helper for a sequence that is not a string.

exemplars.name: ReadBuffer (_typing.py)
exemplars.desc: Typing protocol for readable buffers used by pandas I/O.

exemplars.name: ArrowArrayExportable (_typing.py)
exemplars.desc: Protocol for objects exportable as an Arrow array (PyCapsule interface).

scipy.emphasis: scipy nodes span subpackage modules (stats, signal, optimize, sparse, ndimage, integrate, _lib) and C/Cython-adjacent machinery. Prefer the subpackage in the sentence ("…used by scipy.sparse") because scipy's layout is the main disambiguator. Wrapper/adapter classes are common — say what they adapt.
scipy.glossary: subpackage (stats/signal/optimize/sparse/ndimage/integrate), ndarray, sparse matrix, convolution, filter, distribution fit, solver, numpydoc, callback, wrapper, LowLevelCallable

exemplars.name: LowLevelCallable (_lib/_ccallback.py)
exemplars.desc: Wrapper letting C/Cython callbacks be passed to SciPy routines.

exemplars.name: DisjointSet (_lib/_disjoint_set.py)
exemplars.desc: Union-find (disjoint-set) data structure.

exemplars.name: NumpyDocString (_lib/_docscrape.py)
exemplars.desc: numpydoc parser for a full NumPy-style docstring.

statsmodels.emphasis: statsmodels nodes span regression, tsa (time series), statespace, discrete, stats, and iolib subpackages. Prefer the subpackage in the sentence ("…used by statsmodels.tsa"). Results-wrapper classes are common — describe the result object they wrap (fitted values, parameters, inference).
statsmodels.glossary: regression, time series (ARIMA/SARIMAX/VAR), statespace, MLE, fit, results, formula API, distribution, hypothesis test, prediction, panel

exemplars.name: MLEModel (tsa/statespace/mlemodel.py)
exemplars.desc: Base state-space model estimated by maximum likelihood via the Kalman filter.

exemplars.name: PredictionResults (tsa/base/prediction.py)
exemplars.desc: Wrapper holding out-of-sample prediction values with confidence intervals.

exemplars.name: SimpleTable (iolib/table.py)
exemplars.desc: Formats tabular results as plain text, LaTeX, or HTML for reporting.

scikit-learn.emphasis: ML nodes must be described by their API CONTRACT, not internals. For estimators: fit/predict/transform/score role, what they optimize. Loss classes get math-level one-liners. Never mention C/JNI internals.
scikit-learn.glossary: estimator, fit/predict/transform, hyperparameter search, cross-validation, loss, regularization, kernel, clustering, pipeline, scoring, transformer

exemplars.name: HalfSquaredError (_loss/loss.py)
exemplars.desc: Half squared-error (least-squares) loss.

exemplars.name: PinballLoss (_loss/loss.py)
exemplars.desc: Pinball (quantile) loss for quantile regression.

exemplars.name: BaseEstimator (base.py)
exemplars.desc: Base class for all estimators — provides get_params/set_params and repr.

xgboost.emphasis: Distinguish the high-level Python API (Booster, DMatrix, callbacks, cv, sklearn wrapper) from native-library bindings. Loss classes get math-level one-liners. Never mention C/JNI internals.
xgboost.glossary: Booster, DMatrix, gradient boosting, tree, objective/loss, early stopping, callback, native library, sklearn wrapper, feature importance, prediction

exemplars.name: XGBoostError (_c_api.py)
exemplars.desc: Base exception raised for errors coming from the XGBoost native library.

exemplars.name: TrainingCallback (callback.py)
exemplars.desc: Base class for training callbacks — early stopping, checkpointing, and custom logic.

exemplars.name: compat.py
exemplars.desc: Compatibility shims for optional dependencies (pandas, scipy, sklearn).

lightgbm.emphasis: Distinguish the high-level Python API (Booster, Dataset, callbacks, sklearn wrapper) from native-library bindings. Config/serialization helpers are common.
lightgbm.glossary: Dataset, Booster, gradient boosting, tree, objective/loss, early stopping, native library, sklearn wrapper, feature importance, params

exemplars.name: Dataset (basic.py)
exemplars.desc: LightGBM's internal dataset — bins features and holds labels/weights for efficient training.

exemplars.name: .get() (basic.py)
exemplars.desc: Looks up a parameter value honoring LightGBM's configuration aliases.

exemplars.name: basic.py
exemplars.desc: Module defining the low-level Booster and Dataset wrappers over the native library.

optuna.emphasis: ML/hyperparameter-optimization nodes: describe samplers, pruners, distributions, studies, and integration adapters by their search-contract role. Never mention test harnesses.
optuna.glossary: hyperparameter search, trial, sampler, pruner, study, distribution, objective function, TPE, multi-objective, integration adapter, Gaussian process

exemplars.name: FloatDistribution (distributions.py)
exemplars.desc: A continuous (optionally log-scaled or stepped) float search-space distribution.

exemplars.name: BaseAcquisitionFunc (_gp/acqf.py)
exemplars.desc: Abstract base for acquisition functions used by the Gaussian-process sampler.

exemplars.name: distributions.py
exemplars.desc: Module defining the parameter search-space distributions.

vectorbt.emphasis: Backtesting pipeline actors: describe each node by its ROLE in the backtest flow (accessor, portfolio, signals, indicators, generic machinery) with vectorized/grouped semantics and pandas integration in mind.
vectorbt.glossary: accessor (.vbt), portfolio, signals, indicator, ArrayWrapper, vectorized, grouped, pandas integration, re-wrap, backtest

exemplars.name: ArrayWrapper (base/array_wrapper.py)
exemplars.desc: Wraps a NumPy array with pandas index/columns metadata for named, grouped access.

exemplars.name: BaseAccessor (base/accessors.py)
exemplars.desc: Base for vectorbt's pandas (.vbt) accessors.

exemplars.name: RustSupport (_engine.py)
exemplars.desc: Shim/flag for optional Rust-accelerated routines.

backtrader.emphasis: Event-loop backtesting actors: describe each node by its ROLE in the backtest flow (engine, broker, feed, strategy, analyzer, indicator, commission scheme) using backtrader's own vocabulary.
backtrader.glossary: Cerebro, broker, data feed, OHLCV bar, strategy, analyzer, indicator, commission, order, fill, position, timeframe, session

exemplars.name: Cerebro (cerebro.py)
exemplars.desc: The engine — assembles data, strategies, broker, and analyzers and runs the backtest.

exemplars.name: BackBroker (brokers/bbroker.py)
exemplars.desc: The simulated broker — fills orders and tracks cash, value, and positions.

exemplars.name: TimeFrame (dataseries.py)
exemplars.desc: Enum of bar time frames (Ticks, Minutes, Days, …).

ta-lib.emphasis: INPUT OVERRIDE: the label is a Cython indicator wrapper like "__pyx_pw_5talib_7_ta_lib_19ACCBANDS()"; the payload's name field carries the CLEAN indicator name (e.g. ACCBANDS). Describe the INDICATOR API, never the Cython plumbing — every node is an indicator function. For each indicator write: "<EXPANDED FULL NAME> — <one-sentence functional definition>" (ACCBANDS -> Acceleration Bands; ADX -> Average Directional Movement Index; APO -> Absolute Price Oscillator), stating what it measures or computes at technical-analysis-dictionary level. Always include the full-name expansion — it is the searchable key. Never mention Cython, wrappers, or C internals. LENGTH TIER OVERRIDE: <= 22 words; single sentence, single em-dash.
ta-lib.glossary: moving average, EMA/SMA, oscillator, volatility band, momentum, trend strength, support/resistance, accumulation/distribution, price channels, cycle

exemplars.name: ACCBANDS
exemplars.desc: Acceleration Bands — volatility bands plotted a set factor above and below a simple moving average.

exemplars.name: ADOSC
exemplars.desc: Chaikin A/D Oscillator — the difference between fast and slow EMAs of the Accumulation/Distribution line.

exemplars.name: ADX
exemplars.desc: Average Directional Movement Index — measures trend strength on a 0–100 scale, regardless of direction.

cvxpy.emphasis: cvxpy is a convex-optimization modelling library. Atoms (abs, norm, quad_over_lin), expressions (Variable, Parameter, Expression), constraints (eq, leq, cone), problems (Problem, minimize, maximize), canonicalization/reductions, solvers (SCS, ECOS, OSQP, Clarabel), and lin_ops backends. Describe each node's role in the modelling chain so the sentence is searchable (e.g. "convex atom: absolute value — f(x)=|x|, DCP-compliant").
cvxpy.glossary: DCP, DPP, atom, expression, constraint, canonicalization, reduction, solver, cone, affine, parameter, variable, disciplined convex programming

exemplars.name: Problem (problems/problem.py)
exemplars.desc: cvxpy Problem: holds an objective and constraints; solve() canonicalizes and calls a solver, returning the optimal value.

exemplars.name: Variable (expressions/variable.py)
exemplars.desc: cvxpy Variable: the optimization decision variable with shape and attributes (nonneg, symmetric, PSD...).

exemplars.name: norm (atoms/norm.py)
exemplars.desc: cvxpy convex atom: matrix/vector norm (p-norm, spectral, nuclear) — DCP-compliant.

pyportfolioopt.emphasis: PyPortfolioOpt (pypfopt) does mean-variance portfolio optimization. expected_returns (mean_historical_return, capm_return), risk_models (sample_cov, shrunk_cov), EfficientFrontier (max_sharpe, min_volatility, efficient_return, efficient_risk), Black-Litterman, HRP/HierarchicalRiskParity, discrete allocation (get_discrete_allocation), and CLI helpers. Describe the financial role of each node.
pyportfolioopt.glossary: efficient frontier, Sharpe ratio, covariance, expected returns, Black-Litterman, HRP, discrete allocation, risk model, weight

exemplars.name: EfficientFrontier (efficient_frontier/efficient_frontier.py)
exemplars.desc: pypfopt EfficientFrontier: builds the mean-variance optimizer; max_sharpe()/min_volatility() return the optimal weights.

exemplars.name: mean_historical_return (expected_returns.py)
exemplars.desc: pypfopt expected return estimator: annualized mean of historical price returns.

exemplars.name: sample_cov (risk_models.py)
exemplars.desc: pypfopt risk model: sample covariance matrix of asset returns.

arch.emphasis: arch is a volatility-modelling library (ARCH/GARCH family, unit-root tests, bootstrap). Modules: univariate (ARCH/EGARCH/GJR fits, forecasts), unitroot (ADF/Phillips-Perron/KPSS tests), bootstrap, covariance (CCC/DCC), utility. Note the Cython recursions core is absent — describe the Python API surface around it.
arch.glossary: ARCH, GARCH, EGARCH, GJR, unit root, ADF, Phillips-Perron, KPSS, conditional volatility, resampling, DCC

exemplars.name: ARCH (univariate/volatility.py)
exemplars.desc: arch ARCH/GARCH model class: fit(update_freq=0) returns a results object with conditional_volatility, params, forecasts via forecast().

exemplars.name: ADF (unitroot/stationarity.py)
exemplars.desc: arch ADF unit-root test: returns the test statistic, p-value, and critical values (Engle-Granger style).

exemplars.name: bootstrap (bootstrap/base.py)
exemplars.desc: arch bootstrap: stationary and circular block resampling for confidence intervals on statistics.

alphalens.emphasis: alphalens analyses alpha/factor performance: factor data (FactorData), returns analysis (cumulative returns by quantile), information coefficient (IC) analysis (mean_ic, ic_by_factor), tearsheets, and event studies. Describe each node's role in the factor-research pipeline.
alphalens.glossary: factor, IC, quantile, alpha, tearsheet, cumulative return, factor weight, event study, long-short

exemplars.name: FactorData (alphalens/utils/data.py)
exemplars.desc: alphalens FactorData: wraps factor values + prices + group data; compute_returns() builds forward returns; tear sheet entry point.

exemplars.name: mean_information_coefficient (performance.py)
exemplars.desc: alphalens mean IC over the period with std and IC quantiles — the factor's predictive power summary.

exemplars.name: create_returns_tear_sheet (tears.py)
exemplars.desc: alphalens returns tear sheet: quantile cumulative returns, spread, and turnover plots for a factor.

pyfolio.emphasis: pyfolio builds portfolio tear sheets: returns (create_returns_tear_sheet), positions (create_position_tear_sheet), transactions, benchmark comparisons, drawdown/rolling stats (perf_stats, rolling_sharpe), and round-trip analysis. Describe each function's reporting role.
pyfolio.glossary: tear sheet, drawdown, Sharpe, benchmark, round trip, turnover, positions, transactions

exemplars.name: create_returns_tear_sheet (tears.py)
exemplars.desc: pyfolio returns tear sheet: cumulative returns, drawdown, rolling Sharpe, monthly heatmap, and perf stats in one plot.

exemplars.name: perf_stats (timeseries.py)
exemplars.desc: pyfolio performance statistics table: annual return/vol, Sharpe, Sortino, max drawdown.

exemplars.name: create_full_tear_sheet (tears.py)
exemplars.desc: pyfolio full tear sheet: returns, positions, transactions and round-trip analysis combined.

riskfolio.emphasis: Riskfolio-Lib is a portfolio-optimization suite: Portfolio (mean-variance, tails, constraints via cvxpy), HCPortfolio (HRP/HERC hierarchical clustering), risk measures (MV, CVaR, CDaR, EVaR, MAD), returns estimation, black-litterman, and plotting (risk/return frontier). Note the C++ external bindings are absent — describe the Python API.
riskfolio.glossary: portfolio, CVaR, CDaR, EVaR, HRP, HERC, risk measure, frontier, constraints, black-litterman

exemplars.name: Portfolio (portfolio.py)
exemplars.desc: Riskfolio-Lib Portfolio: builds the optimization problem; optimization() solves it given a risk measure (MV/CVaR/CDaR/EVaR) and constraints.

exemplars.name: HCPortfolio (hcp.py)
exemplars.desc: Riskfolio-Lib HCPortfolio: hierarchical clustering portfolio (HRP/HERC) — linkage + codependence + risk measures.

exemplars.name: returns_estimation (returns.py)
exemplars.desc: Riskfolio-Lib returns estimators: mean/historical/exponential returns for the optimizer input.

shap.emphasis: shap explains model predictions: Explainer (Tree/Linear/Kernel/Deep/Exact), Explanation objects (values, base_values, data), maskers (Independent/Tabular/Partition), plots (summary/force/waterfall/beeswarm/bar), and benchmarking. Note the C++/Cython core (cext/cutils) is absent — describe the Python API surface.
shap.glossary: SHAP, Shapley values, Explainer, masker, base value, feature attribution, waterfall, beeswarm, TreeExplainer

exemplars.name: TreeExplainer (explainers/_tree.py)
exemplars.desc: shap TreeExplainer: exact SHAP for tree ensembles (xgboost/lightgbm/sklearn) with tree_limit and interaction support.

exemplars.name: Explanation (_explanation.py)
exemplars.desc: shap Explanation: the unified output object — values, base_values, data, feature_names; carries .plot().

exemplars.name: waterfall_plot (plots/_waterfall.py)
exemplars.desc: shap waterfall plot: base value to prediction, contributions stacked per feature.

polars.emphasis: polars is the Rust-core DataFrame library; this graph covers the Python API (src layout): DataFrame/LazyFrame/Series, expressions (col/pl.col, filter/group_by/window), IO (read_csv/parquet/scan), datatypes, functions (concat, range), catalog, config. The Rust engine is absent — describe the Python-facing API.
polars.glossary: LazyFrame, DataFrame, expression, group_by, window, scan_parquet, lazy execution, schema, streaming

exemplars.name: DataFrame (dataframe/base.py)
exemplars.desc: polars DataFrame: the eager tabular structure — select/filter/group_by/join; converted from LazyFrame via .collect().

exemplars.name: LazyFrame (lazyframe/base.py)
exemplars.desc: polars LazyFrame: lazy query plan — scan/sink; optimized and executed by .collect()/sink_parquet.

exemplars.name: col (functions/col.py)
exemplars.desc: polars expression constructor: pl.col('name') selects a column into an expression pipeline.

empyrical.emphasis: empyrical is a performance-metrics library (originally from the Quantopian ecosystem): portfolio/strategy performance statistics computed from returns series — annual_return, annual_volatility, sharpe_ratio, sortino_ratio, omega_ratio, calmar_ratio, max_drawdown, alpha/beta vs a benchmark, downside_risk, tail_ratio, information_ratio (IC/IR), stability, perf_attrib decomposition. Modules: stats.py (the metric functions), perf_attrib.py (factor attribution), periods.py (annualization factors), utils.py (helpers), deprecate.py. It is pure Python with no I/O — describe each metric's semantics and its inputs.
empyrical.glossary: Sharpe ratio, Sortino ratio, max drawdown, alpha, beta, information ratio, downside risk, annualization, perf attrib, factor exposure

exemplars.name: sharpe_ratio (stats.py)
exemplars.desc: empyrical sharpe_ratio(returns, risk_free=0, period='daily', annualization=None): computes the annualized Sharpe ratio of a returns series.

exemplars.name: max_drawdown (stats.py)
exemplars.desc: empyrical max_drawdown(returns): returns the largest peak-to-trough drawdown as a positive fraction.

exemplars.name: alpha_beta (stats.py)
exemplars.desc: empyrical alpha_beta(returns, factor_returns): regresses returns on a benchmark factor series and returns (alpha, beta).

empyrical.payload_note: Write exactly ONE semantic sentence per node — a functional summary a quant user can act on. Never produce code; never quote source.

quantstats.emphasis: quantstats is a portfolio analytics + reporting library: statistics (stats.py — sharpe, sortino, cagr, max_drawdown, var, calmar, volatility, skew, kurtosis, win-rate, best/worst day), reports (reports.py — HTML/tear-sheet generation, metrics()/full()/html()), plots (plots.py — returns/drawdown/rolling plots, heatmaps, distribution), montecarlo (simulations, VaR/ES from simulated paths), utils (data helpers, benchmark mapping), _plotting (plotly/matplotlib backends). It depends on empyrical for core metrics. Describe each function's role in the analytics/reporting workflow — what it computes or renders and its key inputs.
quantstats.glossary: Sharpe, Sortino, CAGR, max drawdown, VaR, Calmar, tear sheet, HTML report, benchmark, montecarlo, heatmap, skew, kurtosis, win rate

exemplars.name: metrics (stats.py)
exemplars.desc: quantstats stats.metrics(returns, rf=0, display=True): computes the full metric table (returns, vol, sharpe, sortino, drawdown, var, skew, kurtosis...) as a DataFrame/HTML block.

exemplars.name: full (reports.py)
exemplars.desc: quantstats reports.full(returns, benchmark): builds the complete HTML tear-sheet report (metrics + plots) and renders/saves it.

exemplars.name: html (reports.py)
exemplars.desc: quantstats reports.html(returns, benchmark): returns the HTML string of the full tear-sheet report without rendering.

quantstats.payload_note: Write exactly ONE semantic sentence per node — a functional summary a quant user can act on. Never produce code; never quote source.

yfinance.emphasis: yfinance is a Yahoo Finance data-download client: Ticker (ticker.py — history/fast_info/analysis/calendar/earnings/financials/options/splits/actions/get_info), Tickers (multi-ticker batch), Screener (screener/screener.py — market screeners), search (search.py — symbol search), domain (sector/industry/market classification), scrapers (history/quote/analysis/fundamentals — the HTTP layer), data.py (download() multi-symbol history), shared.py, utils, live.py. Describe each function's client role: what data it fetches and its key parameters. The pricing_pb2.py module is generated protobuf — describe it briefly as the protobuf message layer.

exemplars.desc: yfinance Ticker class: per-symbol client — .history() OHLCV bars, .fast_info for quote snapshot, .info/.get_info() fundamentals, .earnings/.calendar/.analysis.

exemplars.name: download (data.py)
exemplars.desc: yfinance download(tickers, period/interval): batch history fetch across symbols into one DataFrame (MultiIndex columns).

exemplars.name: history (scrapers/history.py)
exemplars.desc: yfinance history scraper: fetches OHLCV price history with period/interval/start/end parameters, returns a DataFrame.
